rationale.conceptual: Implementing the MQM requires understanding of pair fractions, configurational entropy, and polynomial expansions, then setting up a least-squares optimization to fit parameters to experimental phase boundaries. This is an established but non-trivial method in thermodynamics, demanding careful translation of equations into code and proper handling of multiple binary systems simultaneously, rating 3.
rationale.execution: The pipeline consists of two sequential steps: optimize parameters and compute a phase diagram. Both can be accomplished in a single Python script using only numpy/scipy. All experimental data and Gibbs energy values are provided, no external toolchains or complex data fetching required. Straightforward I/O, rating 2.

The method is non-trivial but standard; the pipeline is simple with two sequential steps and provided data. Resources are minimal (CPU-only, tiny data).
